Joyce Center|Purcell Pavilion]] |champion = |tourney = |tourney_result = }} {{2020–21 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2020–21 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Notre Dame]] during the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Fighting Irish were led by 21st-year head coach [[Mike Brey]] and played their home games at the [[Edmund P. Joyce Center|Purcell Pavilion]] in [[Notre Dame, Indiana]] as eight-year members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. The Fighting Irish finished the season 11–15, 7–11 in [[2020–21 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]], to finish in eleventh place. In the [[2021 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] they defeated [[2020–21 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]] before losing to [[2020–21 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] in the second round. They were not invited to either the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] or [[2021 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]]. ==Previous season== The [[2019–20 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Fighting Irish]] finished the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] 20–12, 10–10 in [[2019–20 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a tie for eight place. As the No. 7 seed in the [[2020 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], they defeated [[2019–20 Boston College Eagles men's basketball team|Boston College]] in the second round. The team was scheduled to play [[2019–20 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2020 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] before the tournament was cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web |title=Statement from ACC on Men's Basketball Tournament |url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/3/12/statement-from-acc-on-mens-basketball-tournament.aspx |website=theacc.com |publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference |accessdate=12 March 2020}} The [[2020 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and [[2020 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] were also cancelled due to the pandemic.{{Cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.org/about/resources/media-center/news/ncaa-cancels-remaining-winter-and-spring-championships|title=NCAA cancels remaining winter and spring championships|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200312202043/http://www.ncaa.org/about/resources/media-center/news/ncaa-cancels-remaining-winter-and-spring-championships |archive-date=2020-03-12 |access-date=}} ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" style="text-align:center;" !
